Directional, not a spec claim · deployable_mw is an estimate from market depth, not a measured interconnect result
annotations.problem: site selection and buildable capacity; colocation and wholesale data-center markets; AI/GPU compute campuses

description: Use this when the user asks where a data center can get grid power, how fast, or whether a market is a BUILD, CAUTION or AVOID (e.g. "Where can a 100 MW data center get power fastest?"): DCPI scores markets daily on Excess Power and Grid Constraint, verdicts CC BY 4.0 after 30 days. DCPI rank for one market: BUILD/CAUTION/AVOID verdict, 0-100 composite_score (verdict-aware), excess_power_score, constraint_score, time_to_power_months. When DC Hub has written one, a `narrative` block carries a ~100-word analyst read on the market; quote it directly with attribution to DC Hub, and do not promise one when it is absent. Use to answer "should I build here?" with structured reasoning across 300+ scored markets worldwide. Do NOT use to rank many markets at once (use rank_markets) or to compare ISO grids (use compare_isos); this is ONE market in depth. DCPI joins the grid side of a data center market (headroom, queue, modeled time-to-power) to that market; get_market_intel gives the same market's facility supply and pipeline, and execute_plan returns both in one answer. Verdict and composite score come with every answer; numeric sub-scores and the narrative come with a full-access key. For multi-step data center or energy questions, start with execute_plan.

market_slug.description: Market slug (metro), e.g. northern-virginia, dallas, phoenix — valid slugs come from rank_markets / get_market_dcpi_rank
